record.context_brief: Counting powers in image of c
record.original_question: For c(n) = sum_{k=1}^n 2^{v_2(k)}, define A as the set of exponents a such that 2^a is in the image of c, and define A(x) as the number of a in A with a <= x. Determine the asymptotic behavior of A(x) as x tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Is it possible to make precise the behaviour of A(x) when x -> infinity ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $k$, let $v_2(k)$ denote the 2-adic valuation of $k$ (the largest integer $e\ge 0$ such that $2^e\mid k$). Define
$$c(n)=\sum_{k=1}^{n} 2^{v_2(k)} \qquad (n\ge 1).$$
Let
$$A=\{a\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}: 2^a\in c(\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1})\}$$
be the set of nonnegative integers $a$ such that $2^a$ lies in the image of $c$, and for $x>0$ put
$$A(x)=\#\{a\in A : a\le x\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $A(x)$ as $x\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up any published resolution of the asymptotic behavior of $A(x)$ for the function $c(n)=\sum_{k\le n}2^{v_2(k)}$. No paper, OEIS entry, or problem-tracking page directly addressing this asymptotic was located, so the current status appears unresolved but cannot be confirmed.
